cases.title: SDOT's new signal at Dexter Ave N & John St

source.label: SDOT, Dexter Ave N and John St Traffic Signal Project

cases.question: Does the corner's own record back the signal, and SDOT's numbers?

results.label: Not covered by the evidence
results.why: a new signal is not a federal Proven Safety Countermeasure, so no reduction can be promised

results.label: Cannot test
results.why: the record reads five whole years; SDOT counts three years and one year

results.label: 8 injury crashes
results.why: 88% angle crashes, about $548,000 a year in harm

proof: Seattle's collision records for the corner: 2 in 2023, 14 in 2024, 1 in 2025 (8 with an injury); SDOT's page says 11 in 2024. Both show 2024 as the bad year
cases.fixed: 3 faults this case found: every letter was refused, the memo used the verdict's code, and single-year claims are a written limit
cases.cost: about $0.11 of Meta API for the claim check
cases.summary: SDOT will replace the interim median and crosswalk with a signal, citing 15 collisions in three years, one serious, eleven of them in 2024.

cases.title: NYC DOT's leading pedestrian intervals on Lafayette Street

source.label: NYC DOT to Manhattan Community Board 2, April 28, 2026

cases.quote: Install left turn lane treatment: Plus, Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI): Prince St, Houston St, Great Jones
cases.question: Is each of the three intervals supported by its corner's own crash record?

results.label: Reconsider
results.why: the city's records show an interval already installed there (2024)

results.label: Compare first
results.why: backplates are expected to avoid 0.39 injury crashes a year, against 0.08

results.label: Proceed after a site check
results.why: the estimate holds only if a turning movement is confirmed; 13 injury crashes and 1 death in five years

proof: NYC's own signal dataset (xc4v-ntf4) lists Lafayette Street & Prince Street, installed 2024-10-11, and none at Houston or Great Jones
NYC's crash dataset (h9gi-nx95), by street names: 12 crashes with an injury and 1 with a death at Lafayette & Houston, 13 in all, as the tool says
cases.fixed: 6 faults this case found, all fixed the same day, among them a 2023 death the New York mapping missed
cases.cost: about $0.40 of model use for the whole case

cases.title: Chicago's all-way stop at W 41st St & S Albany Ave

source.label: Chicago City Council, ordinance O2026-0026671 (passed 2026-09-23, 50 to 0)

cases.question: Does the corner's crash record call for the stop the council ordered?

results.label: Not covered by the evidence
results.why: an all-way stop is not a federal Proven Safety Countermeasure

results.label: 1 injury crash in five years
results.why: a quiet corner; the record does not call for the stop, though sight lines or a school might

proof: Chicago's crash dataset (85ca-t3if) by address: 9 crashes at the corner's block numbers since 2021-10-31, 1 with an injury (2026-05-10), as the tool says
cases.fixed: 3 faults this case found, among them every letter refused for naming a fix
cases.summary: The council ordered an all-way stop at West 41st Street and South Albany Avenue.
